$ relay install claude-desktop
exit status 0
--- stdout
# mcpServers.relay-desktop in <TMP>/home/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json:
{
  "command": "<ROOT>/bin/relay",
  "args": [
    "mcp",
    "--host",
    "claude",
    "--desktop"
  ],
  "env": {
    "PATH": "<NODE_DIR>:<TMP>/bin:/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"
  }
}
# relay-desktop is the desktop app's own relay, and is shared. Desktop chats in the main window share one relay process. Cowork, the Code tab's in-app bridge, remote Cowork and widgets share a second. Within each process every conversation carries its own session token, which keeps its jobs, approval requests and events apart from the others'. Code-tab sessions also have their own dedicated relay registration. The token is a bearer key its model holds: it separates conversations that use relay honestly. Configuration describes the topology; doctor does not observe calls or verify which conversation used it. Claude.app 2.42304.0's code was checked on <DATE>: neither process forwards per-conversation metadata. Pass cwd on merge and on starts (a new ask without it consults in a new, empty directory of its own); no session on this shared entry gets an approval dialog, confirm or notices, and its waits end after 50 s, under the app's 60 s tool timeout (README, "Claude desktop app and Cowork").
# <TMP>/home/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json already has relay's entry for this checkout

Nothing to do: relay is already installed for the Claude desktop app from this checkout.
--- stderr

$ relay install claude-desktop --force
exit status 0

$ relay uninstall claude-desktop
exit status 0
--- stdout
# installed <DATE> from <ROOT>/bin/relay, according to <TMP>/home/.config/relay/install.json
#   saved at install, for you to consult: <TMP>/home/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json.bak-relay
# remove mcpServers.relay-desktop from <TMP>/home/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
$ rm <TMP>/home/.local/bin/relay

Nothing was changed. Re-run with --write to apply.
Start the app again: open -a Claude

Not removed, because it can hold your work or your logins:
  <TMP>/home/.local/state/relay (not present)
      relay's state: the registry of runs, logs, the prompts sent and the transcripts
  <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay/worktrees (not present)
      the worktrees of write jobs
  <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay/consult (not present)
      the directories questions without a project were asked in
  <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay/harness (not present)
      the state of the harnesses relay confines itself (each item's Copilot, Grok or Gemini home)
  <TMP>/home/.config/relay
      your relay configuration, its local settings (local.json), the installation record and what install saved
  <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay-codex-home (not present) [holds a login (auth.json)]
      relay's Codex home: the Codex login relay's jobs run on, and their Codex sessions
  <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay-codex-pins (not present)
      relay's pinned Codex releases (sealed read-only, so they are made writable first) and the qualifier's results
  <TMP>/home/.config/relay-keys (not present) [holds API keys]
      the API key files relay hands a key-only target (Gemini); local.json can name a key file elsewhere, which is yours to delete
  <TMP>/home/.relay-t (not present)
      relay's private sockets and per-turn state
  <TMP>/home/.rn (not present)
      the short temp directories relay gives Claude's turns
  <TMP>/home/.rsm/q (not present)
      the Codex qualifier's scratch runs
  in each repository relay ran a write job in: the line `.relay/` in .git/info/exclude, and any relay/* branches

To remove them by hand, in this order:
  1. <ROOT>/bin/relay clean
     First, while the state directory is still there. It commits work left in finished jobs' worktrees to
     their branches, removes those worktrees, and deletes relay/* branches that are already merged. It lists
     the unmerged branches it kept, so no work is lost.
  2. In each of those repositories: `git branch --list 'relay/*'` shows what is left. Merge what you want,
     delete the rest with `git branch -D <branch>`, and delete the line `.relay/` from .git/info/exclude.
  3. Stop the Codex qualifier's LaunchAgent, if you installed it:
     # none found in ~/Library/LaunchAgents; if you installed one under another name: launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/<label>, then delete its plist and <TMP>/home/Library/Logs/relay-codex-qualifier
  4. Then the rest, after checking each: the ones marked above hold credentials.
     rm -rf <TMP>/home/.local/state/relay
     rm -rf <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay/worktrees
     rm -rf <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay/consult
     rm -rf <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay/harness
     rm -rf <TMP>/home/.config/relay
     rm -rf <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay-codex-home
     chmod -R u+w <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay-codex-pins && rm -rf <TMP>/home/.local/share/relay-codex-pins
     rm -rf <TMP>/home/.config/relay-keys
     rm -rf <TMP>/home/.relay-t
     rm -rf <TMP>/home/.rn
     chmod -R u+w <TMP>/home/.rsm/q && rm -rf <TMP>/home/.rsm/q
--- stderr
